headline: BNP nominates Mirza Fakhrul as presidential candidate, he resigns from party posts
summary: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has stepped down as BNP Secretary General and Standing Committee member after being nominated for the 23rd President of Bangladesh.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has resigned from his positions as Secretary General and member of the Standing Committee of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). He submitted his resignation to Party Chairman Tarique Rahman on Thursday afternoon.
The resignation follows his nomination by the BNP to contest for the 23rd President of Bangladesh. According to the constitution, he must vacate his party posts to run for the presidency.

A BNP delegation, led by Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, submitted Fakhrul's nomination papers to the Election Commission (EC) on Thursday. Dr. Abdul Moin Khan and Gayeshwar Chandra Roy served as the proposer and supporter, respectively.

Fakhrul will face competition from Oli Ahmed Bir Bikram, who is backed by an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami. The alliance stated they fielded a candidate to ensure a contested election rather than an uncontested victory.
The election schedule stipulates that nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16, and the last date for withdrawal is August 18. The voting will take place on August 20.
This marks the first time in 35 years that a presidential vote will be required due to multiple candidates. Members of Parliament will cast their votes in the National Parliament session.
Given the BNP's two-thirds majority, Fakhrul is widely expected to be elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh.
caption:
BNP has nominated Mirza Fakhrul for the presidency. He has already resigned from his party posts to contest the race.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has resigned from his positions as Secretary General and member of the Standing Committee of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). He submitted his resignation to Party Chairman Tarique Rahman on Thursday afternoon.

The resignation follows his nomination by the BNP to contest for the 23rd President of Bangladesh. According to the constitution, he must vacate his party posts to run for the presidency.

A BNP delegation, led by Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, submitted Fakhrul's nomination papers to the Election Commission (EC) on Thursday. Dr. Abdul Moin Khan and Gayeshwar Chandra Roy served as the proposer and supporter, respectively.

Fakhrul will face competition from Oli Ahmed Bir Bikram, who is backed by an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami. The alliance stated they fielded a candidate to ensure a contested election rather than an uncontested victory.

The election schedule stipulates that nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16, and the last date for withdrawal is August 18. The voting will take place on August 20.

This marks the first time in 35 years that a presidential vote will be required due to multiple candidates. Members of Parliament will cast their votes in the National Parliament session.

Given the BNP's two-thirds majority, Fakhrul is widely expected to be elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud takes [[6 for 55 to bowl out Australia]] for 198 in Darwin
headline: Hasan Mahmud takes 6 for 55 to bowl out Australia for 198 in Darwin
summary: Hasan becomes the first Bangladeshi bowler to claim a five-wicket haul in Australia, leading the Tigers' pace attack to a dominant opening day.
details: Hasan Mahmud made history in Darwin, claiming a career-best 6 for 55 from 17 overs to bowl Australia out for 198 on the opening day of the first Test at Marrara Stadium.
With this performance, Hasan became the first Bangladeshi bowler to ever take a five-wicket haul on Australian soil, surpassing Mashrafe Bin Mortaza's previous best of 3 for 74 in 2003.
Hasan's success came through relentless consistency, repeatedly challenging the off-stump channel to dismiss key batters including Travis Head, Pat Cummins, and Mitchell Starc.
He further dismantled the lower order, dismissing Steve Smith and Nathan Lyon to wrap up the Australian innings.
The Tigers' pace attack dominated the day, with Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain contributing two wickets each to account for all 10 Australian wickets.
This marks only the second time in Test history that Bangladesh's pacers have taken all 10 wickets in an innings, following a similar feat against Pakistan in 2024.
Former Australian opener David Warner praised the visitors' accuracy, noting it was the first time he had seen an opposition team hit their mark so effectively upon arriving in Australia.
caption:
History made in Darwin! 🇧🇩

Hasan Mahmud becomes the first Bangladeshi to take a 5-wicket haul in Australia.

Hasan Mahmud made history in Darwin, claiming a career-best 6 for 55 from 17 overs to bowl Australia out for 198 on the opening day of the first Test at Marrara Stadium.

With this performance, Hasan became the first Bangladeshi bowler to ever take a five-wicket haul on Australian soil, surpassing Mashrafe Bin Mortaza's previous best of 3 for 74 in 2003.

Hasan's success came through relentless consistency, repeatedly challenging the off-stump channel to dismiss key batters including Travis Head, Pat Cummins, and Mitchell Starc.

He further dismantled the lower order, dismissing Steve Smith and Nathan Lyon to wrap up the Australian innings.

The Tigers' pace attack dominated the day, with Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain contributing two wickets each to account for all 10 Australian wickets.

This marks only the second time in Test history that Bangladesh's pacers have taken all 10 wickets in an innings, following a similar feat against Pakistan in 2024.

Former Australian opener David Warner praised the visitors' accuracy, noting it was the first time he had seen an opposition team hit their mark so effectively upon arriving in Australia.
